topic: Mechanical remote controls system: Teleflex, Bowden and use of control tube and cables
syllabus_extract: Mechanical remote controls system: Teleflex, Bowden and use of control tube and cables
specific_objectives: 17.1.5.1 Trainee will be able to explain the construction and functioning of aircraft flight controls systems and its components.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of Bowden cable tensioning and control tube routing; Safety: Wear gloves to prevent cable pinch injuries; Instructor supervision: Monitor trainee handling of tensioning tools
intro_questions: What is the primary function of a mechanical remote control system?
Name two types of mechanical remote control systems used in aircraft.
Why is a control tube required in a Bowden cable system?

topics: Differences between Bowden and Teleflex systems
development.content:
Bowden cable construction and components
Teleflex cable construction and components
Functioning of Bowden cable mechanism
Functioning of Teleflex cable mechanism
Differences between Bowden and Teleflex systems

Control tube construction and purpose
Cable routing and termination methods
Tensioning procedures and adjustment
Inspection criteria for control cables
Maintenance and lubrication requirements

topics: Common failures in remote control systems
development.content:
Common failures in remote control systems
Troubleshooting mechanical control issues
Safety considerations during maintenance
Documentation and reporting procedures
Integration with other control systems

summary_questions: Explain the role of the control tube in a Bowden cable system.
Describe the key differences between Bowden and Teleflex cable constructions.
List three critical inspection points for aircraft control cables.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the principles of Bowden and Teleflex systems apply to the next lesson on specific control system components (LP 23).
